$comment: Shared VfTabs cases. Plain data only: no Vue, no PHP, no renderer objects. Each adapter maps these neutral fields onto its own API. The vocabulary is the historical Vue contract at fd793696f50d3be0fcd3788f0f8f751c63869963. The third catalog for a component that owns controls, and the first whose controls carry an explicit interactive role (tab), a roving tabindex, aria-selected and a relationship graph with a 0-or-1 panel: every case declares `componentInteractive` - one tab per item plus the two scroll buttons of every instance, plus the active panel when a panel slot exists and an item is active - and `consumerInteractive` for a consumer control before the tabs or inside the panel slot. An interaction case names the gesture, the semantic effect it must produce on every target - selection, aria-selected, tabindex, panel, focus, indicator, scroll state, prevented keys and the event log as separate claims - and the initial case whose DOM the result must converge on, or `postOnly` with the reason a scrolled viewport has no fresh render. scripts/ci/tabs-coverage.mjs is what stops the list eroding.

propVocabulary.items: VfTabItem[], required. Each item is { value, label, disabled?, tabId?, panelId? }. Rendered in order as button.vf-tabs__tab[role=tab][type=button] inside div[role=tablist]; disabled writes the native attribute; tabId and panelId override the generated ids.
propVocabulary.modelValue: string | null | undefined, default undefined. The controlled value; wins whenever defined, an empty string included, and null falls through to the seed. A Vue consumer pairs it with update:modelValue (v-model). The Razor adapter reads it as the initial value and selects on its own.
propVocabulary.defaultValue: string | undefined. Seeds the uncontrolled state once; an unknown or disabled value is kept as-is.

contentVocabulary.panel: The panel slot, rendered for the active tab only: `text` followed by the active value in a paragraph, so the slot's activeValue is visible; `control` is a real consumer button inside the panel. Its presence is what makes every tab write aria-controls.
contentVocabulary.tab: The tab slot: `numbered` renders "N. Label" for each item, so the slot's item and index are visible. Static per item on every target; the isActive slot prop is Vue-only and pinned by the characterization suite.
contentVocabulary.before: A consumer control rendered as a sibling *before* the tabs root, inside the case: `control` is a real consumer button, the origin of the native Tab scenario.

groupVocabulary: A list of sibling tabs rendered side by side in one case, each with its own props; the case-level props are ignored, the content applies to each. Values may be shared: the reference focuses through the instance's own refs, so nothing depends on document order.

ownershipVocabulary.componentInteractive: The exact number of controls the component itself renders in this case: one button.vf-tabs__tab per item and the two scroll buttons of every instance (hidden or shown), plus one div.vf-tabs__panel[tabindex=0] per instance that has a panel slot and an active item. Asserted on every target against the measured component-owned controls, their tag identity and the explicit `tab` role against the profile.
ownershipVocabulary.consumerInteractive: The exact number of consumer controls in the case: one for a `before` control, one for a `panel.control` when the panel is rendered.

interactionVocabulary.$comment: A case with an `interaction` is driven in the browser with real pointer and key events, then re-measured: the snapshot, the DOM and the accessibility tree are all taken again. The snapshot waits, bounded, for the scroller's 140 ms scrolling state to end.
interactionVocabulary.steps: clickButton (a real pointer click at the element's centre; `selector` is .vf-tabs__tab, a scroll button, or a consumer control class; `index` picks a match in document order across every instance), focusButton (`selector` and `index` likewise), pressKey with Enter, Space, Tab, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home, End or PageDown.
interactionVocabulary.expect: Claims checked against the snapshot on every target. `activates` is whether a native click reached a tab - true for a pointer click on a tab and for Enter/Space, false for every handled navigation key and for a scroll-button click. `selectedValue` is the value of the first selected tab of the first instance (null when none), `selectedValues` the same per instance, `ariaSelected` and `tabindexes` the per-tab attributes of the first instance, `disabledValues` the tabs with the native attribute. `panelPresent` and `panelLabelledByActive` describe the panel of the first instance. `focusRole` is tab, panel, scroll-left, scroll-right, body, other-inside-case or outside-case; `focusValue` the focused tab's value; `focusInstance` which instance holds it. `indicatorOpacity`, `indicatorTransform` and `indicatorWidth` are the inline declarations, unrounded. `scrollLeft`, `canScrollLeft`, `canScrollRight`, `leftHidden`, `rightHidden`, `leftAriaHidden`, `rightAriaHidden`, `leftTabindex`, `rightTabindex`, `leftDisabled`, `rightDisabled`, `fades`, `scrolling`, `scrollbarWidth` and `settled` are the scroller state. `keydownPrevented` is whether each keydown was prevented, in order. `events` is the neutral change log the fixture keeps. A key of the form `a11y:<role>.<state>` is a claim about the accessibility tree read after the action; Chrome 153 exposes `selected` for role=tab, so the selection is claimed there as well as in the DOM.
interactionVocabulary.matches: The initial case whose DOM the post-interaction DOM must equal on the same target. Every tab persists across a selection change and the panel is patched, so the result of a gesture has to be exactly the DOM a fresh render of the target state produces.
interactionVocabulary.postOnly: The reason a scenario names no `matches`: only for a viewport left scrolled, which no server render can express. Such a scenario must claim scrollLeft and the scroller state absolutely.

cases.title: Nothing given, no panel slot: the first item is selected, no aria-controls, no panel
cases.$why: The fallback itself, and the no-panel half of the relationship contract: every tab has an id and no aria-controls, and nothing carries role=tabpanel.

cases.title: A panel slot: every tab writes aria-controls, the active panel exists with aria-labelledby and tabindex=0
cases.$why: The panel half. Two of the three aria-controls references dangle by design: only the active panel is rendered.

cases.title: defaultValue seeds the middle tab
defaultValue seeds the last tab
A controlled modelValue selects the middle tab
A controlled modelValue selects the last tab
modelValue wins over a different defaultValue
An unknown controlled value: no tab selected, every tabindex -1, no panel, hidden indicator
cases.$why: The roving tabindex is a projection of the value, not an invariant: zero tabs are tabbable here, on every target.

cases.title: An empty-string controlled value selects nothing
cases.$why: The ?? boundary: an empty string is a value.

cases.title: A null modelValue falls through to defaultValue
cases.$why: Null is an absence for rendering. The Vue side is still controlled for emitting, which the characterization suite pins.

cases.title: A disabled first item: the fallback skips it
A disabled middle item beside the selected first one
A disabled middle item with the last one selected
A disabled last item
A disabled last item with the middle one selected
defaultValue names a disabled item: it stays selected, tabbable, with its panel
cases.$why: Selected is value equality alone. The disabled tab carries aria-selected=true and tabindex=0 and its panel is rendered.

cases.title: Every item disabled: no selection, no panel
No items: an empty tablist, no panel, hidden indicator
cases.$why: Zero tabs, two scroll buttons, no panel: the ownership budget is 2. Not photographed: a zero-height list has nothing to clip.

cases.title: One item, selected
Two items share a value: duplicate ids, two selected tabs, two tabindex=0, one panel
cases.$why: The pathology the reference produces and a port would be tempted to normalise: the first two tabs carry the same id, the same aria-controls, aria-selected=true and tabindex=0; the panel is the first occurrence's.

cases.title: An item with its own tabId: the tab id and the panel aria-labelledby use it
An item with its own panelId: the tab aria-controls and the panel id use it
A panelId item without a panel slot: aria-controls on that tab only, no panel
cases.$why: An external panel the consumer renders elsewhere. The reference writes the reference without the panel; the other tabs write nothing.

cases.title: A value with a space is embedded into the ids unchanged
A tab slot replaces the label: numbered content receives item and index
A consumer class after the canonical class and a consumer style on the root
Consumer id, data-testid and aria-label forwarded onto the root
dir=rtl on the root: the tabs lay out right to left
dir=rtl with the middle tab selected
dir=rtl with the last tab selected
Four items overflow the 360px case: right button shown, right fade, indicator on the first tab
cases.$why: The overflow state at scrollLeft 0: can-scroll-right on the list, the right button visible and tabbable, the left one hidden, aria-hidden, tabindex -1 and disabled, one fade, and the indicator unclipped.

cases.title: The selected last tab is partly under the right scroll button: the indicator is clipped to the visible span
cases.$why: A fractional, clipped indicator: the tab starts inside the viewport and ends beyond the button, so the width is the visible span and the offset is the tab's own.

cases.title: Seven items: a long overflow at scrollLeft 0
The selected last of seven items is entirely out of view: opacity 0, width 0, offset kept
cases.$why: The clipped-to-nothing case: the indicator keeps the tab's offset and hides. A port that kept it visible, or reset the offset, differs in the inline style.

cases.title: Seven items under dir=rtl: the left button is the one shown, the left fade, and the LTR-frame indicator
cases.$why: The scroller reads the direction and mirrors its state; the indicator does not, and computes its offset from the list's left edge in the LTR frame - the historical quirk, reproduced on every target.

cases.title: Two instances sharing values, the second seeded to the middle tab: separate ids, separate selection
cases.$why: Shared values between siblings are honest here: the reference focuses through its own refs, so nothing depends on document order. Ten component-owned controls: six tabs, four scroll buttons - plus two panels.

cases.title: Two instances both on the middle tab
Two instances, the first on the middle tab
A consumer button before the tabs, with the middle tab selected
cases.$why: The consumer control that Tab starts from in tabs/interaction-tab-into-list: the roving tabindex is proved by where native focus lands.

cases.title: A consumer button inside the panel slot
cases.$why: A consumer control inside component-owned markup: counted as the consumer's, never as the component's, and never as a tab.

cases.title: A real pointer click on the middle tab selects it: aria-selected, tabindex, panel, indicator move; one change
A click on the current tab changes nothing and still emits the pair
cases.$why: No "already current" guard: the reference emits update:modelValue and change again. A port that suppressed the re-activation fails on the event log.

cases.title: Two clicks: the panel is patched twice, the log has both values in order
Enter on a focused, unselected tab activates it natively: one click, keydown not prevented
cases.$why: No Enter handler: the browser synthesises the click. A port that handled Enter itself would prevent the keydown or count two activations.

cases.title: Space on a focused, unselected tab activates it natively
ArrowRight from the first tab: prevented, the next tab selected and focused
ArrowLeft from the middle tab
ArrowDown moves forward on the horizontal tablist
cases.$why: The vertical pair is handled although the tablist is horizontal. A port that followed the ARIA pattern instead of the source would leave this key to the page.

cases.title: ArrowUp moves backward on the horizontal tablist
Home from the last tab selects and focuses the first
End from the first tab selects and focuses the last
ArrowRight from the last tab wraps to the first
ArrowLeft from the first tab wraps to the last
ArrowRight skips the disabled middle tab
ArrowLeft skips the disabled middle tab
End lands on the last enabled tab
PageDown is left to the page: not prevented, nothing changes
A disabled tab refuses focus, so a key pressed after it reaches nothing
cases.$why: button.focus() on a disabled button is a no-op, so focus stays on the body and the keydown never reaches a tab.

cases.title: Focusing an unselected tab changes no state: focus and selection are two halves
Navigation starts from the focused tab, not the selected one: ArrowLeft from a focused last tab lands on the middle
cases.$why: From the selected first tab ArrowLeft would wrap to the last; from the focused last tab it goes to the middle. Only the second is the reference.

cases.title: Tab from the selected tab moves native focus to the panel: not prevented, nothing selected
cases.$why: Tab is unhandled. The panel carries tabindex=0, so it is the next tabbable element after the tablist.

cases.title: Tab from a consumer button before the tabs lands on the selected (tabindex 0) tab, skipping the first
cases.$why: The roving tabindex proved by native focus movement: the first tab has tabindex -1 and is skipped, the selected middle tab has 0 and receives focus. A target whose tabindex was inverted or all-zero fails on where focus lands.

cases.title: ArrowLeft under dir=rtl moves forward
ArrowRight under dir=rtl moves backward and wraps
A v-model consumer: the click emits, the consumer writes the value back, the selection moves
cases.$why: The controlled protocol round-tripped through a consumer that accepts. The Razor adapter has no parent to ask and selects directly; all three land on the same state.

cases.title: A click in the second instance moves only its selection and its panel
cases.$why: Two instances sharing values: the state, the events and the focus stay in the instance that was clicked. selectedValue and the per-tab arrays describe the first instance; selectedValues describes both.

cases.title: ArrowRight in the second instance: its selection and its focus move, the first is untouched
cases.$why: Focus isolation with shared values, honest in the catalog: the reference focuses through the instance's own refs.

cases.title: A click on the partly visible last tab selects it: the indicator is clipped to the visible span after the move
cases.$why: Post-selection indicator geometry under clipping, converging on the same state rendered fresh.

cases.title: The right scroll button scrolls the four-item list to its end: the left button shows, the right hides, the selected first tab is clipped by the left button
cases.$why: The scroll step is max(120, round(360 * 0.6)) = 216, clamped by the 38px of overflow. The snapshot waits for the 140 ms scrolling state to end before measuring; scrolling and scrollbarWidth are claimed settled.

interaction.postOnly: A scrolled viewport cannot be rendered fresh by the server: scrollLeft is browser state. The absolute claims here stand in for convergence.

cases.title: The right scroll button scrolls the seven-item list by 216px: both buttons, both fades, the selected first tab hidden under the left button
cases.$why: The selected tab is entirely to the left of the shown left button: opacity 0 at the button's inset, width 0.

interaction.postOnly: A scrolled viewport cannot be rendered fresh by the server.

cases.title: Right then left returns the seven-item list to its start and converges on the initial render
cases.$why: The one scroll scenario with an honest convergence target: two opposite steps land on scrollLeft 0, which is the fresh render. Focus stays on the left button the pointer pressed, which is hidden again - a hidden control keeps focus until it moves.

cases.title: A click on the consumer button inside the panel changes nothing of the tabs
cases.$why: The consumer control stays the consumer's: no tab event, no selection change, focus reported as inside the case but on no tab.
